title: Pythagorean Theorem in Hyperbolic and Spherical Geometry
description: What's the analog of the Pythagorean theorem in hyperbolic and spherical geometry? Formalize cosh(c) = cosh(a)*cosh(b) and cos(c) = cos(a)*cos(b), unified via curvature.

insights: Hyperbolic Pythagorean theorem: cosh(c) = cosh(a)*cosh(b) for right triangle with legs a,b and hypotenuse c
Spherical Pythagorean theorem: cos(c) = cos(a)*cos(b) on the unit sphere with sides in (0, pi/2)
General radius version: cos(c/R) = cos(a/R)*cos(b/R) on sphere of radius R
Unified curvature framework via generalizedCos(kappa, x): cos(sqrt(kappa)*x) for kappa>0, cosh(sqrt(-kappa)*x) for kappa<0, 1 for kappa=0
Flat limit: both non-Euclidean laws reduce to a^2 + b^2 = c^2 as curvature -> 0, via Taylor expansions
Hyperbolic angular defect: area = pi/2 - alpha - beta > 0; spherical excess: area = alpha + beta - pi/2 > 0
Law of cosines connection: both spherical and hyperbolic laws reduce to Pythagorean form when angle C = pi/2
cosh is strictly increasing on [0, infinity), enabling uniqueness of complementary leg
Proved HasDerivAt for cosh and sinh at zero for flat-limit analysis
All 50+ theorems proved from Mathlib trig/exp library with no axioms
